subject: botany_2
question_text: What is EcoRI? How does it function?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.45, printed question 110. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK ERROR, corrected on this card: the guide says EcoRI "recognises GAA sites". EcoRI recognises the SIX-base palindrome GAATTC and cuts between G and A. The guide's own LAQ answer on p.16 prints GAATTC correctly, so it contradicts itself.

insider_note: GAATTC, not GAA. Write the six bases out, on two strands, and the cut position is obvious.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What EcoRI is
steps.margin_note: The enzyme class, the source, and the naming convention.
lines: It is obtained from the bacterium ESCHERICHIA
The name is read: E from the genus Escherichia,
co from the species coli, R from the strain, and
I because it was the first such enzyme isolated
steps.why: The naming convention says exactly where an enzyme came from, so a name like EcoRI is a short address rather than an arbitrary label.
common_mistakes: Saying EcoRI is an exonuclease. It is an ENDOnuclease — it cuts WITHIN the DNA.
Not explaining the name. The convention is worth one line.
steps.memory_tip: Genus, species, strain, order of discovery.

steps.label: How it cuts
steps.margin_note: Write both strands with the cut marked, then say sticky ends.

lines.text: 5'  G ↓ A A T T C  3'
3'  C T T A A ↑ G  5'

lines: It cuts between G and A on BOTH strands.
The cuts are staggered, so each piece is left
with a short single stranded overhang — a
steps.why: Cutting off-centre on both strands leaves overhangs that can base pair with any other fragment cut by the same enzyme, which is what makes joining possible.
common_mistakes: Writing GAA as the recognition site. It is GAATTC, six bases. The guide's VSAQ answer is wrong here.
Saying the cut is straight across. It is STAGGERED, which is what makes the ends sticky.
steps.memory_tip: Six bases, cut off-centre, sticky ends both sides.
